newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Bank stocks take hit on Argentine bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Bank stocks take hit on Argentine bolsa.

text.p: Argentina's Banco Frances and Banco Galicia dived in early trading Thursday on the Buenos Aires bolsa, hurt by interest rate jitters and sell programs, dealers said.

"People think the results of banks will reflect the negative impact of the climb in U.S. long bond yields over the past 10 or 15 days, because local banks have large bond holdings," said analyst Juan Pablo Paillot at brokers Ravello.
A trader at a leading bank also blamed the fall on sell programs.
Banco Frances reeled 3.7 percent and Banco de Galicia fell 2.2 percent on the bolsa, compared with drops of 3.6 percent and 3.3 percent, respectively, in their ADRs.
The banks were among only a handful of blue chip stocks trading on the bolsa two hours after the official opening time, with the weighted MerVal index .MERV shedding 0.5 percent to 709.48.
"The bolsa is getting off to a very late start because of tension ahead of the release of the U.S. producer price index Friday," the trader said.
He said this uncertainty was weighing down Argentine Brady bonds, even though the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond yield ticked only a fraction lower to 7.12 percent Thursday.
"Everybody is closely watching the long bond yield to try to gauge the tone on Wall Street," Paillot said.

Traders said banks might even be affected by the plunge of nearly 30 percent in the ADR of Pepsi bottler Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA on Wall Street, which defaulted on a $500 million loan earlier this month. "Banks are creditors of Baesa and investors fear it may not be able to meet other debt obligations," another trader said.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, however, said in a report Thursday it remained bullish on the banking sector and reiterated its buy recommendation for Banco Frances.

"The trend in the Argentine banking system is towards strong volume growth rather than margin expansion. Therefore, if the U.S. Federal Reserve increases rates by a further 25 basis points or 50 bp DMG predicts no significant impact on the cost of funds or loan growth for Frances," DMG said.
It expected the bank to see 28 percent growth in deposits and loans in fiscal year 1997 and a 30 percent rise in 1998 as 56 new branches are opened.
